terms.meaning: Python's built-in way to save an object to a file and read it back, which can run code if the file is tampered with.
A plain text format for structured data that many tools can read.
A named setting held by the operating system that programs can read, such as the API key.
A text file of named settings that the app can read, kept out of shared code.
A definition of the shape a piece of data must have, such as a project.

pptx, langchain_openai, langchain_chroma, pdfplumber, openpyxl (checked by the environment check)

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and shared data model
sections.what: Loads the standard tools and the project data model that the helpers work with.
sections.why: Likely reason: the helpers need to know the shape of a project to save, read, and summarize it.
sections.watch_out: Every helper depends on the project data model, so renaming it breaks all of them.

sections.name: save_project
sections.title: Saving a project to a file
sections.what: Writes the project into the output folder. If no name is given, it builds one from the project name and the time. It returns the file path.
sections.why: Likely reason: saving lets a user keep work and reopen it later.
sections.watch_out: The cleaning of unsafe characters applies only when no name is passed, so a name supplied by the caller is used as is.

sections.name: load_project
sections.title: Reopening a saved project
sections.what: Reads a saved project file and returns the project as it was stored.
sections.why: Likely reason: it pairs with saving so work can be resumed.
sections.watch_out: Pickle files can run code when opened, so only open files this app created.

sections.name: list_saved_projects
sections.title: Listing saved projects with readable names
sections.what: Finds saved project files in the output folder, newest first, and gives each a readable name and a date.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets a user choose a project from a list.
sections.watch_out: The name is rebuilt from the file name, so names with extra underscores may look odd, and the date is the file's last-change time, not the save time.

sections.name: format_evidence_for_display
sections.title: Summarizing source evidence for display
sections.what: Turns a list of supporting excerpts into a short numbered list, showing at most five and noting how many are left out.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the display readable when there are many matches.
sections.watch_out: Excerpts are cut at 200 characters without regard to word boundaries.

sections.name: format_reasoning_for_display
sections.title: Formatting an agent's reasoning trace
sections.what: Builds a readable report of one agent's run, including its name, time, duration, confidence, input, evidence, steps, and output.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the owner judge how an agent reached its result.
sections.watch_out: Only the first three evidence items are shown, and the report fails if the timestamp is missing.

sections.name: validate_environment
sections.title: Checking settings and folders
sections.what: Checks for the API key, the env file, the data folders, and required packages. It returns whether the setup is valid, with errors and warnings.
sections.why: Likely reason: catches common setup mistakes before the app runs.
sections.watch_out: It does not load the env file itself, so the key check sees only variables that were already loaded elsewhere.

sections.name: get_color_scheme
sections.title: Named color palettes for charts
sections.what: Returns one of three named color sets for charts, and falls back to the first set when the name is unknown.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives charts a consistent look without repeating color codes.
sections.watch_out: A misspelled name silently returns the default set, so the mistake is not reported.

sections.name: truncate_text
sections.title: Cutting text to a set length
sections.what: Shortens text to a given length and adds dots when it is cut.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps labels and cells from overflowing.
sections.watch_out: Very small limits can leave almost no text because the dots take up space.

sections.name: format_duration
sections.title: Turning weeks into readable time
sections.what: Converts a number of weeks into words such as one week, three weeks, or about two months.
sections.why: Likely reason: plans are easier to read in months once they pass a month.
sections.watch_out: Months are counted as four weeks each, so the month figure is an estimate.

sections.name: calculate_project_metrics
sections.title: Totals and risk counts for a project
sections.what: Counts workstreams, modules, and activities, reads the durations and any time saved, and counts activities marked high risk.
sections.why: Likely reason: summary screens and reports need these numbers in one place.
sections.watch_out: Assumes each risk level has a value field and that durations are filled in, so missing data gives errors or zeros.

sections.name: export_to_json
sections.title: Writing project data to a JSON file
sections.what: Writes the whole project to a readable JSON file in the output folder and returns the file path.
sections.why: Likely reason: JSON can be read by other tools and by people.
sections.watch_out: Uses an older model conversion method that may fail or warn with newer versions of the data library.

sections.name: print_project_summary
sections.title: Printing a project overview to screen
sections.what: Prints the project's counts, timeline, savings, structure, risk count, confidence, and last-modified time in one block.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives a quick check from the command line.
sections.watch_out: Crashes if the last-modified time is missing, and shows savings only when an optimized duration exists.

summary: A set of shared helper functions for saving, loading, listing, formatting, checking, and summarizing the proposal project.
purpose: Hold common tasks in one place so the rest of the app can reuse them.
why: Likely reason: the code groups repeated work into shared helpers. The code does not state the reason directly.
how: Saving writes the project to a pickle file in the output folder. Loading reads that file back. Listing scans the output folder for saved projects. Formatting helpers turn evidence, reasoning, durations, and text into readable strings. The environment check looks for the API key, the data folders, and required packages. Metrics count the parts of a project. The export writes JSON. The summary prints a short overview.
inputs: Project objects, file names, the output folder, a color scheme name, week counts, text, and reasoning or evidence records.
outputs: File paths, a loaded project, lists of saved projects, dictionaries of checks and metrics, formatted strings, and printed output.
risks: Loading a pickle file can run harmful code if the file was altered, so only trusted files should be opened. A filename passed in is used without cleaning. The environment check does not load the env file itself. The JSON export uses an older model conversion call that may stop working with newer data library versions. The summary print fails when the last-modified time is missing. Metrics assume risk levels have a value field.
debug: For saved file problems, check the output folder and confirm the file came from this app. For JSON export failures, check the version of the data library. If the key check reports missing, confirm the env file was loaded. If metrics show zeros, check that the project fields are filled. If the summary print crashes, check the last-modified value.
